conclusion:
MEASURED on the exp60 ins35 bed (56 clips, official metric; base reproduced exactly: ALL 0.93988, div 25/31/74). As ORACLES, yes: the three together give more than +0.01, and they add up slightly better than the plain sum. FP-fork removal + gated orphan attach + no-node relink = +0.02056 pooled (44b6 +0.0235, 6bba +0.0201, div 32/0/67, 44 clip wins/0 losses). The sum of the singles is +0.00629 + 0.00541 + 0.00734 = +0.01904. With the wide attach pool the joint is +0.04115, against a sum of +0.03402.
Super-additivity comes almost entirely from the division Jaccard J = TP/(TP+FP+FN). Base is 25/130 = 0.1923. Removing the 31 FP forks shrinks the denominator to 99, so each attached TP is then worth 0.1/99 = +0.00101 instead of 0.1/130 = +0.00077. Example: FP alone gives 25/99, +0.00602. Gated ATT alone gives 32/130, +0.00538. Together they give 32/99 = 0.3232, +0.01309, which is +0.00169 more than the sum. That is exactly the measured FP+ATT_g excess. FP+LINK is slightly sub-additive (-0.00017) because both act on edge FP and LINK already removes one FP fork. LINK+ATT is roughly additive.
Two corrections to the round-11 ceilings. (a) The gated attach ceiling +0.0054 is confirmed (7 TP). The wide pool with GT picks has 26 TP, not 17, so its ceiling is +0.0204, not +0.0131. (b) 'Links <= +0.003' only holds for end->free-start links: +0.0003 attach-only, +0.0011 with the 25 both-matched removals. The full no-node relink oracle is +0.0073, and 85% of that (+0.0062) comes from 129 SWAPS. In a swap, a matched track end u's true successor v is already linked to an unmatched neighbour track w: |wv| median 1.6 um versus |uv| 7.3 um, and w has a parent in 94% of cases. So the ILP gave the closer, unannotated neighbour the link during fast motion. A looser info ceiling removes every official FP edge (1,651 of 1,676 have one end unmatched), which needs knowledge of which cells are annotated. It gives +0.0646 alone, and +0.111 with wide attach.
What this means for the bar: the joint CEILING is 1.7x (gated) to 3.4x (wide) the +0.012 lab bar. To clear the bar, a real mechanism would have to capture about 58% of the gated joint, or about 29% of the wide joint, at near-zero added error. The realistic versions measured so far all lose or do nothing. Orphan attach: -0.0129 (mirror, 3.4% precision) and -0.0273 (nearest, 2.4%); break-even for an added fork is ~26.5% precision. Fork removal: 0 for 5 on the LB. The swap relink would need to tell a 7 um true move from a 1.6 um neighbour without GT, and no such cue has been measured. So the answer to 'three together = +0.01?' is: as a ceiling, yes, about +0.021 (up to +0.041). As a realizable gain, nothing measured gets there. With the ~1/6 lab-to-public transfer, even a perfect gated joint would be about +0.003 public.
